finding_quote: The second model call did not return within the 300 s budget (`TimeExceeded`).
reason: I checked CTV-9CE7EA/run-003. mini-swe-agent.traj.json has info.model_stats.api_calls = 1 and exit TimeExceeded. There is one assistant turn at 12:16:17.71Z, 5.5 s after execution_timer_started_at 12:16:12.221Z (commands.log), with 3 tool calls (grep, defects4j test, find). All 3 returned code 0, but all 3 results are stamped 12:21:17.07Z, which is 304.85 s after the start. The ledger has api_calls 1 and final_gap_s -4.9. In the instance's other runs (001, 004, 005, 006) every batch with a defects4j test returned in 0.52 to 0.57 s. In mini-swe-agent default.py, query() raises TimeExceeded before n_calls += 1 and model.query, so no second call was made. driver_mxF0.log puts the launch at 12:16:09Z. Run-002's stall ran 11:49:28 to 12:05:34. The 574 s probe ended at 12:15:08, and three fast probes (5.6, 4.0, 5.8 s) passed just before launch. The record therefore shows no provider latency in this run. This one edit also carries the fixes for the overlapping findings: the stall-rule finding, the inference-lens finding on the same bullet, and consistency finding #1.

edits.old:
- The agent's first model call issued three commands, which completed. The second model call did not return within the
    300 s budget (`TimeExceeded`).
  - Stall rule 2 did not apply, because less than 60 s of budget remained after the last tool result.
  - It occurred at 12:16Z, in the same window as a provider stall (run-002 at 12:05Z) and a 574-second health probe (12:15Z).
edits.new:
- The run made one model call (api_calls = 1). It returned 5.5 s after the timer started, with three commands (grep,
    `defects4j test`, find). All three exited 0, but their results were recorded only at 304.9 s, 4.9 s after the 300 s
    budget had expired, so the agent stopped (`TimeExceeded`) before any second model call. In this instance's other runs,
    batches containing a `defects4j test` call returned in about 0.5 s. The cause of the delay in the tool step is not
    recorded.
  - Neither stall rule applied: rule 1 needs at most 2 commands (the run issued 3), and rule 2 needs more than 60 s of
    budget left after the last tool result (the final gap was -4.9 s).
  - It launched at 12:16:09Z, after run-002's provider stall (11:49Z to 12:05Z) and a 574-second health probe (ended
    12:15:08Z), but three fast probes (4.0 to 5.8 s) passed just before launch and its one model call returned in 5.5 s, so
    the record shows no provider latency in this run.

finding_quote: Stall rule 2 did not apply, because less than 60 s of budget remained after the last tool result.
reason: In scripts/ct_status.py classify(), rule 1 is stall = api_calls<=2 and commands<=2. The run had 3 commands, so rule 1 fails. Rule 2 needs the last event to be a tool result with final_gap > 60. Here final_gap is -4.9, so no budget was left at all. The report leaves out rule 1 and understates the gap. The fix is part of the combined edit under the first finding ('Neither stall rule applied: ...').

reason: The trajectory of CTV-065313/run-002 shows that tool call 10 was `find /private/tmp /usr /opt -type f \( -name 'junit-4*.jar' -o -name 'junit.jar' \) 2>/dev/null | head -20`. Its only output line was /private/tmp/ct3ws-diagF1/.../CTV-BEE8CB/lib/junit.jar, which the 'junit.jar' pattern matched. The command as the report quotes it could not have produced that path.

finding_quote: This is a disclosed residual risk to cost, not to data validity.
reason: In scripts/scan_v3.py, any call's output triggers contamination on NARROW (gold_rank, gold_methods, structured_submission, variant_manifest, cue-trust-v3, mechanism-search, VARIANT_KEY, the repo path), on foreign CTV ids or on cross-level cue tokens. After a flagged call it also triggers on MARK or pristine-only lines. There is no pattern for gold method names, and a display carrying none of these markers would pass. The dash-encoded claude-501 path does not contain the repo path or 'mechanism-search'. Agents do search /tmp outside their workspace (CTV-065313/run-002, and CTV-E72EE8/run-003 runs `find /tmp`), and mx_tmp_audit.py skips claude-*. 'Not to data validity' therefore overclaims. X7's 'so the data stay valid' and X2's 'out-of-workspace source' have the same problem. A grep of all 148 recorded trajectories finds no access to claude-501, which I added as the supported mitigating fact.

edits.old:
workspace. The frozen scanner stops any run that displays out-of-workspace harness content or another variant id
  (X2 showed that it does), and such a run is excluded.
- **Conclusion.** This is a disclosed residual risk to cost, not to data validity.
edits.new:
workspace. The frozen scanner stops any run whose output shows another variant id, a harness marker, the experiment name
  or the repository path, or, after an out-of-workspace call, a pristine-only source line (X2 showed the variant-id check
  working), and such a run is excluded. It does not match gold method names as such, so a gold name shown without any of
  these markers would not be stopped.
- **Conclusion.** This is a disclosed residual risk. Most exposures would be stopped and cost a run, but the scanner does not
  catch every possible display, so some risk to data validity remains. No recorded trajectory shows access to
  `/private/tmp/claude-501`.

edits.new:

  run if its output showed a pristine-only line, a harness marker or another variant id, and every stop costs a run. Source
  shown without any of these would not be caught, so a residual validity risk remains.
